| [NOTE-1811](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1811.md) | Herrmannsdoerfer, Benz and Juergens — COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models | When a modeling language's metamodel changes, the existing models must be migrated. The paper calls this pairing "coupled evolution". **The requirements study.** An earlier study of two industrial metamodel histories found: - about half the changes were metamodel-only; - more than three quarters of the coupled changes were metamodel-independent, so they could be reused; - the rest were metamodel-specific; - none were model-specific. This yields two requirements: reuse and expressiveness. **COPE's answer.** A language evolves through a sequence of coupled transactions, each pairing a metamodel adaptation with its model migration. | Read |

| [NOTE-2350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2350.md) | Freeman and Pfenning — Refinement Types for ML | Refinement types narrow ML's types without changing its programs. The programmer declares recursive subtypes of a datatype; these close under intersection and union into a finite lattice; inference is abstract interpretation over it, after ML inference, and decidable because the lattice is finite and only refinements of one ML type are intersected. An expression has σ ∧ τ when it has both. Annotations are accepted only when the inferred refinement already lies below them. Soundness is stated and its proof omitted. | Read |
| [NOTE-2351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2351.md) | Davies and Pfenning — Intersection Types and Computational Effects | Intersection types, which refinement types need because one function has several properties, are unsound with mutable references. Restricting intersection introduction to values and dropping distributivity restores soundness, with a proof. Inference being most likely undecidable and principal types absent, the paper gives a bidirectional checker: types are ascribed by the programmer, mostly to function definitions, checked against and passed down to subterms, synthesized where they can be read off, and erased. No rule changes a term or inserts a coercion. | Read |
| [NOTE-2353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2353.md) | Rondon, Kawaguchi and Jhala — Liquid Types | Liquid types are dependent types {ν : B \| φ} whose predicates, wherever a type must be inferred, are conjunctions of logical qualifiers from a finite set the programmer supplies. Inference runs Hindley-Milner, generates subtyping constraints over templates, and weakens an assignment of every qualifier to the strongest conjunction the constraints allow, under a conservative implication check in a decidable logic. Checking and inference are decidable; a program with no liquid type is reported, and nothing in the program is changed. | Read |
